vision.one_liner: Open-source fleet management for small businesses — see your vehicles, track your maintenance, own your data.
vision.tagline: Fleet management that doesn't charge you per van.

target_audience.primary: Small business owners with 5-50 light commercial vehicles
target_audience.persona: Owner-operator who manages the fleet themselves alongside 12 other jobs

differentiators: Open source — no per-vehicle SaaS fees
Self-hosted — your data stays on your server
No hardware lock-in — works with any GPS source
Simple UX — designed for owner-operators, not enterprise fleet managers
Built-in simulator — try it without owning a fleet
vision.competitive_positioning: Nextcloud for fleet management. Credible open-source alternative that gives small operators enterprise-grade capability without enterprise pricing or complexity.

feature_areas.name: GPS Ingestion, Trip Detection & Simulator
feature_areas.summary: REST API for GPS data, movement-based trip detection, route visualization, simulator as V1 data source

feature_areas.name: Maintenance & Service Management
feature_areas.summary: Service schedules (mileage/time), alerts, history with cost tracking, fleet-wide overview

feature_areas.name: Driver Management & Auth
feature_areas.summary: Admin + driver roles, assigned and pool vehicle models, vehicle history per driver, privacy controls

feature_areas.name: Inspections & Compliance
feature_areas.summary: Custom checklist templates, pre/post-trip inspections, photo capture, compliance calendar, audit trail

definition_of_done: docker compose up gets a working product with simulated fleet
Live map shows simulated vehicles moving in real-time
Driver can log in, see their vehicle, complete an inspection
Admin can see fleet dashboard, drill into any vehicle, view trips on map

performance.realtime_latency: <5s for vehicle position updates via WebSocket
performance.gps_ingestion: Handle 50 vehicles at 1 position per 10 seconds

security.privacy: Tracking schedule, end-shift toggle, driver data export/delete

design_standards.navigation: Sidebar nav for admin, simplified nav for driver
design_standards.three_click_rule: All key journeys reachable in 3 clicks or fewer

vehicle_status.orange: Requires attention — service approaching, document expiring, minor alert
vehicle_status.red: Overdue — past service interval, outside leasing terms, compliance failure

design_standards.map: Dominant element on dashboard (~70% width), collapsible status sidebar (~30%)

voice_and_tone.direct: Say what the thing does, no jargon
voice_and_tone.practical: Every element should be useful or get out of the way
voice_and_tone.gut_check: Would a plumber with 8 vans know exactly what this means?

po_checks: Can I see all my vehicles on a map right now?
Can I click a vehicle and see its details without leaving the map?
Can I tell which vehicles need attention (service, inspection, documents)?
Can I see where a vehicle went yesterday?
Can a driver log in and only see their vehicle?
Can a driver complete a pre-trip checklist on their phone?
Can I see the maintenance history and costs for any vehicle?
Does the simulator make the product feel real without owning a fleet?
Can I deploy this with a single docker compose up?
Is my data on my own server, not someone else's cloud?

FA1.name: Fleet Dashboard & Live Map

user_journeys.name: View live fleet map
user_journeys.steps: Owner opens app → sees live map with all vehicle positions → vehicles color-coded by traffic light status (green/orange/red) and motion state (moving/idle/parked)

user_journeys.name: Inspect vehicle from map
user_journeys.steps: Owner clicks vehicle marker on map → popup shows vehicle name, driver, status, speed, last trip, traffic light, any alerts → link to full vehicle detail view

user_journeys.name: Review fleet status sidebar
user_journeys.steps: Owner glances at sidebar → sees vehicles due for service (count + list), overdue inspections, expiring documents, active alerts sorted by urgency

user_journeys.name: Filter map by status
user_journeys.steps: Owner filters map → by traffic light status, by driver, by motion state (moving/idle/parked)

acceptance_criteria: Map loads in <2s with 50 vehicle markers
Vehicle positions update in real-time via WebSocket (<5s latency)
Vehicle markers show direction of travel when moving
Vehicle markers color-coded by traffic light status
Sidebar shows top-priority alerts sorted by urgency
Map remembers zoom level and center between sessions
Responsive: usable on tablet with sidebar collapsing to bottom sheet
Clicking vehicle marker opens popup with key stats and link to detail
Map clusters markers at low zoom levels

FA2.name: Vehicle Registry & Detail View

user_journeys.name: Add a vehicle
user_journeys.steps: Owner clicks Add Vehicle → enters make, model, year, VIN, license plate, color, current odometer, photo → saves

user_journeys.name: View vehicle detail
user_journeys.steps: Owner opens vehicle from list or map → sees tabbed view with Overview, Trips, Maintenance, Inspections, Documents

user_journeys.name: Check vehicle health at a glance
user_journeys.steps: Overview tab shows traffic light indicator, current location on mini-map, assigned driver, odometer, key stats

user_journeys.name: Change vehicle status
user_journeys.steps: Owner edits vehicle status → active, in-shop, decommissioned → decommissioned vehicles hidden from map/dashboard by default

acceptance_criteria: Vehicle list supports search, sort (name, status, mileage, next service), and filter
Vehicle list shows traffic light indicator per row (worst status across maintenance, inspections, documents)
Vehicle detail loads all tabs without page refresh
Traffic light: green = all clear, orange = requires attention, red = overdue/compliance failure
Vehicle photo upload supported
Decommissioned vehicles hidden from map and dashboard by default, visible via filter
Vehicle detail overview shows mini-map with current position

FA3.name: GPS Ingestion, Trip Detection & Simulator

user_journeys.name: Simulator feeds fleet data
user_journeys.steps: Simulator service runs → generates realistic GPS coordinates for N configured vehicles → POSTs to ingestion API → vehicles appear on map moving along roads

user_journeys.name: System detects trip start
user_journeys.steps: Vehicle moves >5km/h for >30s → system creates trip record → trip appears in vehicle's trip list as 'active'

user_journeys.name: System detects trip end
user_journeys.steps: Vehicle stationary for >3min → system closes trip → calculates distance (from GPS points, not straight-line) and duration

user_journeys.name: View trip on map
user_journeys.steps: Owner opens vehicle → Trips tab → clicks trip → sees route line on map with start/end markers, timestamps, distance, duration

user_journeys.name: Browse trip history
user_journeys.steps: Owner views trip list for a vehicle → filters by date range → sorts by distance or duration

acceptance_criteria: GPS ingestion API: POST endpoint accepting lat, lon, speed, heading, timestamp, vehicle_id
Positions stored with PostGIS geometry type
Trip detection runs as background process, <30s from trip end to record creation
Trip start threshold: speed >5km/h for >30s (configurable)
Trip end threshold: stationary for >3min (configurable)
Minimum trip distance: 200m to filter GPS drift (configurable)
Trip distance calculated from actual GPS points along route
Trip route rendered as polyline on map with start/end markers
Simulator configurable: number of vehicles, speed profiles, trip patterns
Simulator generates routes that follow roads (not random straight lines)
Simulator runs as a Docker Compose service alongside app and db

FA4.name: Maintenance & Service Management

user_journeys.name: Create service schedule
user_journeys.steps: Owner creates service schedule for a vehicle → selects type (oil change, tires, brakes...) → sets interval by mileage OR time OR both → sets estimated cost

user_journeys.name: Receive service alert
user_journeys.steps: System detects service approaching threshold (e.g., 500mi before due, 2 weeks before) → alert appears on dashboard sidebar and vehicle detail

user_journeys.name: Log completed service
user_journeys.steps: Owner logs service → date, odometer, cost, vendor, notes, receipt photo → service record added to history → next service due recalculated

user_journeys.name: View maintenance history
user_journeys.steps: Owner opens vehicle → Maintenance tab → sees chronological history filterable by type → running cost total

user_journeys.name: Fleet-wide maintenance overview
user_journeys.steps: Owner opens Maintenance from sidebar → sees what's due this week/month across all vehicles → sorted by urgency

acceptance_criteria: Service schedules support mileage-based, time-based, or dual triggers
Alerts fire at configurable warning thresholds (e.g., 500mi before, 2 weeks before)
Maintenance cost tracking with per-vehicle and fleet-wide totals
Common service types pre-populated (oil, tires, brakes, filters, fluids, belts, battery)
Custom service types supported
Receipt photo upload on service records
Completed service resets the schedule countdown automatically

FA5.name: Driver Management & Auth

user_journeys.name: Create driver profile
user_journeys.steps: Owner creates driver → name, phone, email, license number, license expiry, photo → driver receives login credentials

user_journeys.name: Assign driver to vehicle (assigned model)
user_journeys.steps: Owner assigns driver to vehicle → one driver per vehicle at a time → assignment history tracked

user_journeys.name: Driver logs in (assigned model)
user_journeys.steps: Driver logs in → sees their assigned vehicle → current status, next service due, pending inspections → tracking-active indicator visible

user_journeys.name: Driver checks into pool vehicle
user_journeys.steps: Driver logs in → sees available vehicles list → picks one → system creates temporal assignment → pre-trip inspection prompted

user_journeys.name: View driver history
user_journeys.steps: Owner opens driver detail → sees all vehicles they've driven, duration per vehicle, assignment history

acceptance_criteria: Two roles: admin (owner/manager) and driver
Driver sees only their assigned vehicle(s)
Assignment history tracked with timestamps (who drove what, when)
License expiry alerts surface on dashboard and driver list
Driver login works on mobile browser (responsive)
Pool mode: driver selects from available vehicles, temporal assignment created
Assigned mode: driver sees their primary vehicle on login
First-login privacy notice shown and must be acknowledged before tracking begins
Tracking-active indicator visible in driver UI at all times when tracking is on
End-shift toggle available to driver — stops tracking until next shift
Tracking schedule configurable by admin (e.g., 07:00-18:00 Mon-Fri) — on by default
Per-driver data export (JSON/CSV) for GDPR right of access
Per-driver data hard delete for GDPR right to erasure

FA6.name: Inspections & Compliance

user_journeys.name: Create inspection template
user_journeys.steps: Owner creates template → name, list of check items (tires, lights, brakes, fluids, seatbelt...) → assigns to vehicle type

user_journeys.name: Driver completes pre-trip inspection
user_journeys.steps: Driver opens inspection → sees checklist → marks each item pass/fail/NA → adds notes and photos for failures → submits

user_journeys.name: Admin reviews inspections
user_journeys.steps: Owner views inspections → sees pass rate, outstanding failures → clicks inspection to see detail with photos

user_journeys.name: Compliance tracking
user_journeys.steps: System tracks inspection frequency per vehicle → alerts if vehicle hasn't been inspected on schedule → compliance view shows current/overdue status

acceptance_criteria: Customizable checklist templates with different templates per vehicle type
Photo attachment on failed inspection items
Inspection history per vehicle with pass/fail summary
Compliance view: which vehicles are current vs overdue on inspections
Inspection submissions timestamped and immutable (audit trail)
Inspection frequency alerts configurable (e.g., daily pre-trip required)
Disclaimer: not a tachograph, ELD, or DVIR-compliant system

factory_decisions.decision: Use localStorage for map view persistence with key 'openfleet-map-view'
factory_decisions.context: AC requires map to remember zoom and center between sessions. localStorage is the simplest client-side persistence that survives page reloads and browser restarts.
alternatives_considered: URL hash params (clutters URL, shared links change view)
factory_decisions.rationale: localStorage is the boring technology choice (McKinley). No server-side state needed for a per-browser preference. JSON-serialized {center, zoom} with validation on load to handle corruption.

factory_decisions.decision: Save on moveend event (not zoomend separately)
factory_decisions.context: MapLibre fires moveend after both pan and zoom operations complete. Using moveend alone covers both cases without double-saving.
alternatives_considered: Debounced save on any map interaction
factory_decisions.rationale: moveend fires after zoom changes too, so a single handler is sufficient and simpler. No debounce needed — localStorage writes are synchronous and cheap.

factory_decisions.decision: Search Before Building audit for cycle 1 story map-persistence
factory_decisions.rationale: Found: 1 BUILD (persistence utils), 1 EXTEND (FleetMap component). Key reuse: FleetMap already has map init logic — extended with saved state restore. map-utils.ts already has shared utilities — added persistence functions alongside existing helpers.

factory_questions.question: Spec says 'WebSocket' but SSE was used instead. The <5s latency AC is met. Should future stories continue with SSE or switch to WebSocket via custom server?
factory_questions.found_in: story map-realtime AC: Vehicle positions update in real-time via WebSocket (<5s latency)
factory_questions.resolved_as: Proceeded with SSE. Functionally equivalent for server-to-client push. Logged as divergence.

acceptance_criteria: Map remembers zoom level and center between sessions

divergences.spec_says: Vehicle positions update in real-time via WebSocket (<5s latency)
divergences.actually_did: Used Server-Sent Events (SSE) instead of WebSocket. SSE endpoint at /api/positions/stream pushes position updates to clients with EventSource auto-reconnection.
divergences.rationale: Next.js 14 App Router does not support WebSocket upgrade in route handlers. SSE achieves identical real-time push semantics with <5s latency, simpler architecture (no separate WS server), native browser reconnection via EventSource, and compatibility with HTTP/2. For a one-way server-to-client push (positions), SSE is the boring technology choice (McKinley principle).
affects_acceptance_criteria: Vehicle positions update in real-time via WebSocket (<5s latency)

findings: 18-model Prisma schema covers all 6 feature areas: User, Session, Vehicle, Position, Trip, DriverAssignment, ServiceType, ServiceSchedule, MaintenanceRecord, InspectionTemplate, InspectionTemplateItem, Inspection, InspectionResponse, Document, Alert, AuditLog, Setting.
FA1 (Dashboard/Map): Vehicle, Position, Alert — all present with trafficLight, motionState fields.
FA2 (Vehicle Registry): Vehicle with all required fields (make, model, year, vin, licensePlate, color, photoUrl, status, odometer) — present.
FA3 (GPS/Trips): Position (lat, lon, speed, heading, timestamp, vehicleId), Trip (distance, duration, start/end coords, isActive) — present.
FA4 (Maintenance): ServiceType, ServiceSchedule (mileage/time/dual triggers, warnings), MaintenanceRecord (cost, vendor, receiptUrl) — present.
FA5 (Driver Auth): User with role enum (ADMIN/DRIVER), licenseNumber, licenseExpiry, privacyAckedAt. DriverAssignment with type (ASSIGNED/POOL), temporal tracking — present.
FA6 (Inspections): InspectionTemplate, InspectionTemplateItem, Inspection with result enum (PASS/FAIL/NA), InspectionResponse with photoUrl — present.
All foreign keys properly defined with onDelete: Cascade. Indexes on query-hot columns (vehicleId+timestamp, userId+isActive, severity+isDismissed, etc.).
No feature area would need ALTER TABLE to function. Schema is complete for all 6 FAs.
PostgreSQL + PostGIS: docker-compose.yml uses postgis/postgis:16-3.4 image. Prisma schema enables postgis extension. Connection via env var DATABASE_URL — no hardcoded credentials.
Prisma ORM: Client generated with postgresqlExtensions preview. Global singleton in src/lib/db.ts prevents connection exhaustion in dev. Seed script present.
iron-session: Session wrapper in src/lib/session.ts. Uses env var SESSION_SECRET with dev fallback. Cookie config: httpOnly, sameSite:lax, secure in production, 7-day TTL.
GPS Ingestion API: POST /api/positions with Zod validation, batch support, vehicle existence check, motion state auto-update. 16 tests passing.

GPS Simulator: Configurable via env vars (API_URL, VEHICLE_COUNT, INTERVAL_MS). Generates Bristol-area GPS coordinates with speed profiles (urban/suburban/highway), trip state machine, heading-based movement. Resolves vehicle IDs from API.
MapLibre GL JS: Installed as dependency but not initialized — documented as blocking_gap. Map rendering is FA1 scope, not foundation scope. ACCEPTABLE.
Health check endpoint: GET /api/health verifies database connectivity.
Login: POST /api/auth/login — validates with Zod, finds user by email, bcrypt.compare password, saves session with userId/role/name. Returns 401 on invalid credentials.
Logout: POST /api/auth/logout — calls session.destroy(). Clean implementation.
Session check: GET /api/auth/me — returns session data or 401.
Session persistence: iron-session with 7-day TTL, httpOnly cookie, sameSite:lax.

Protected routes: Admin layout (src/app/(admin)/layout.tsx) checks session — redirects to /login if unauthenticated, redirects to /driver if not ADMIN. Driver layout (src/app/(driver)/layout.tsx) mirrors with DRIVER check, redirects to /dashboard if not DRIVER.
Role-based access: ADMIN and DRIVER roles enforced at layout level. requireAdmin() and requireDriver() helpers in src/lib/auth.ts.
Login page: Client component with form, error handling, loading state, role-based redirect after login.
Password hashing: bcrypt with 12 rounds in auth.ts, 10 rounds in seed (acceptable for dev data).
14 auth tests passing.

5 alerts at varying severity (INFO, WARNING, CRITICAL) — tire rotation, battery check, MOT expiring, insurance renewal, inspection overdue.
4 app settings: tracking schedule, data retention, company name, timezone.
No placeholder data — all emails, phone numbers, VINs, license plates are realistic and domain-appropriate.

analysis_recommendation.rationale: Confidence 0.75 with 5 quality gaps concentrated in S3-fleet-dashboard UX states (loading/error/empty). All map-core functional ACs pass. Gaps are bounded, addressable without new capabilities, and stem from product-standard requirements not decomposed into story ACs. Deepen to add UX polish before promoting map-core milestone.

analysis_result.recommendation_reasoning: PO Review verdict is NEEDS_IMPROVEMENT with confidence 0.75. All 4 map-core stories are done and all functional ACs pass. The 5 quality gaps are UX polish items (loading skeleton, error boundary, empty state, SSE reconnect UI, perf benchmark) — all concentrated in S3-fleet-dashboard. Root cause for all 5 is missing_context: the product standard requires loading/error/empty states handled, but no map-core story AC specified them. These are bounded changes (3 medium, 2 low priority) addressable without new capabilities. The 2 low-priority gaps (SSE reconnect UI, perf benchmark) require staging/browser infrastructure not yet available — defer those. Deepen with the 3 medium-priority UX state gaps to bring dashboard to product-standard quality before promoting map-core.

integration_gaps: PostGIS geometry columns deferred to FA3 — positions stored as float lat/lon. Documented trade-off, not blocking map-core.
silent_degradation: SSE used instead of WebSocket — documented divergence with rationale. Functionally equivalent for server-to-client push.

root_cause_analysis.gap_description: Add loading skeleton for map container during tile fetch
root_cause_analysis.evidence: Product standard requires loading_states_handled: true. No map-core story AC specified loading states. The builder implemented what was specified. A different builder would make the same omission.

root_cause_analysis.gap_description: Add error boundary around FleetMap with retry UI
root_cause_analysis.evidence: Product standard requires error_states_handled: true. No map-core story AC specified error boundaries. The ErrorBoundary component exists in shared UI (foundation) but was not wired into FleetMap.

root_cause_analysis.gap_description: Add empty state message when no vehicles have positions
root_cause_analysis.evidence: Product standard requires empty_states_handled: true. No map-core story AC specified empty state behavior. The EmptyState component exists in shared UI (foundation) but was not wired into the dashboard map flow.

root_cause_analysis.gap_description: Add visual feedback for SSE disconnect/reconnect
root_cause_analysis.evidence: No AC or spec language mentions reconnection UI. EventSource provides native auto-reconnect but no user-facing feedback was specified. Product standard visibility-of-system-status heuristic expects this.

cross_cycle_patterns.pattern: Product standard UX requirements (loading/error/empty states) not decomposed into story ACs
cross_cycle_patterns.systemic_cause: Story decomposition does not cross-reference product_standard.quality_standards.reliability against each story's affected_screens to generate UX state ACs
cross_cycle_patterns.recommended_action: Instruct story-building phase to include loading, error, and empty state ACs for every story that adds a new screen or component. These are product-standard requirements, not optional polish.

change_spec_briefs.what_good_looks_like: Map container shows a loading skeleton (pulsing placeholder matching map dimensions) while tiles load. Skeleton disappears when map fires 'load' event. User sees immediate visual feedback that the map is loading.
change_spec_briefs.approach_hint: Add a loading state to DashboardMap that shows before FleetMap mounts. Use MapLibre 'load' event to transition. The Loading component from foundation can be used, or a skeleton div with animate-pulse.

change_spec_briefs.what_good_looks_like: If FleetMap throws (WebGL unsupported, tile load failure), an error boundary catches it and shows a retry button with a helpful message. The rest of the dashboard remains functional.
change_spec_briefs.approach_hint: Wrap FleetMap in the existing ErrorBoundary component from foundation shared UI. Add a map-specific fallback message. Test with a deliberately failing map initialization.

change_spec_briefs.what_good_looks_like: When no vehicles exist or none have positions, the map area shows an empty state message: 'No vehicles to display. Add vehicles to see them on the map.' with a link to /vehicles. Follows the EmptyState component pattern from foundation.
change_spec_briefs.approach_hint: Check vehicles array length in DashboardMap. If empty, render EmptyState component instead of FleetMap. The EmptyState component already exists in shared UI with title, description, and optional action link.

phase_decisions.reasoning: Confidence 0.75 is below the 0.90 threshold for promote. Although all map-core functional ACs pass and the evaluator noted gaps 'belong to dashboard-features or as polish stories', the product standard explicitly requires loading/error/empty states. These are 3 bounded changes that bring the milestone to standard quality. Promoting now would carry forward gaps that are cheaper to fix in the map-core context than in dashboard-features.
alternatives_considered: promote — rejected because confidence < 0.90 and 3 medium-priority product-standard gaps remain
notify-human — not warranted, gaps are well-understood and bounded
